plain_english_policy: This bill makes it a criminal offense (a Class C misdemeanor) to violate specific administrative rules created by the State Forestry Commission regarding how people behave on state-owned forest land.
policy_direction_if_enacted: Enactment would establish new criminal penalties for violations of forestry conduct rules within designated state forests, thereby increasing legal consequences for non-compliance with commission regulations in that jurisdiction.
sponsorship_supports_position: The sponsor advanced this legislation to amend the Code of Alabama regarding state forestry penalties.
evidence_quotes: "This bill would provide that a violation of certain administrative rules promulgated by the State Forestry Commission and pertaining to the conduct of persons on land designated as a state forest is a Class C misdemeanor."
"Unless otherwise provided by law, a violation of a rule adopted by the commission pertaining to the conduct of persons on land designated as a state forest shall be a Class C misdemeanor."
